integration_issues.issue: After clearing browser cookies and revisiting /checkin/:token in the same Playwright context, the page rendered the checkin-already state instead of the expected checkin-needs-login state. Could be a Playwright cookie-timing artifact (next test step — fresh login as member — DID correctly clear and show checkin-not-admin, suggesting clear_cookies works). Recommend main agent self-verifies in an incognito browser tab: open https://club-express-lite.preview.emergentagent.com/checkin/<token> with no session — should show the amber 'Admin login required' card with the checkin-go-login button routing to /login?next=/checkin/<token>.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~6152 lines — even further past the 700-line guideline. Strongly recommend splitting into route modules (auth, members, events, rsvp_checkin, photos, chat, gear, payments, admin, emails). Same recommendation as iter-13/14/15.

send_rsvp_ticket_email regenerates ticket_id with str(uuid.uuid4()) if rsvp.get('ticket_id') is missing (line ~1529). For RSVPs created BEFORE the qrcode patch, this means each email send produces a DIFFERENT QR — so a re-sent email becomes a different ticket and the original QR a member already screenshotted is invalidated. Recommend: backfill missing ticket_id onto the RSVP doc instead of generating ephemeral ones inside the email function.

/checkin/scan/{token} accepts any token signed with JWT_SECRET regardless of issued_at age — there is no 'exp' claim. Long-lived tickets are fine for events, but consider validating event.end_at hasn't passed before allowing scan, OR setting exp = event.end_at + 24h at make_ticket_token time. Otherwise a stale QR from a year-old event can be scanned again.

checkin_scan has no rate limit. A malicious admin (or a leaked admin session) could brute-force ticket_ids by signing tokens with the public JWT_SECRET — but JWT_SECRET should never be exposed; if it ever leaks, every ticket becomes forge-able. Recommend rotating JWT_SECRET on a schedule + considering a separate TICKET_SECRET key.

CheckinScan.jsx line ~62 short-circuits the dispatch effect when status is success/already/error — correct. But there is no `not_admin` short-circuit, which means if AuthContext re-fires `user` change while in not_admin state the effect re-runs and could flip status to checking_in. Minor.

GuestIn.ticket_type defaults to 'general' silently. No allow-list validation against {vip, all_access, general, guest, speaker, volunteer} — a malicious payload could store ticket_type='admin' or any free-text. Recommend Pydantic Literal[...] or validator.
